overall_structure.value: Multiphase microstructure of the 600 °C annealed 35 h milled Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 powder: BCC (ferrite) as the major phase plus partially ordered B2, a small amount of γ-brass type and the newly evolved Fe5Si3-type silicide (hP16) intermetallic; a nanocrystalline structure is retained after annealing.

unmapped_findings: The 35 h milled parent powder is thermally stable up to ~500 °C; the Fe5Si3-type silicide phase forms at ~520 °C (evident as an exothermic event) and its diffraction peaks are evolved at 600 °C and grow further up to 800 °C.

DTA of the 35 h milled powder shows exothermic events at ~420 °C (attributed to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase) and ~520 °C (attributed to formation of the Fe5Si3-type/Fe3Si-type intermetallic).

Rietveld-refined lattice parameters and volumes of the phases in the 600 °C annealed sample (Table 4): BCC a = 0.286 nm (V = 23.39 Å³); γ-brass type a = 0.872 nm (V = 663.05 Å³); B2 a = 0.289 nm (V = 24.13 Å³); Fe5Si3 type a = b = 0.667 nm, c = 0.466 nm (V = 179.54 Å³).
The Fe5Si3-type silicide forms due to undissolved Si remaining after milling and the tendency of Fe and Mn to react with Si, the binary mixing enthalpy between Fe–Si and Mn–Si being highly negative.
The theoretical melting point of the HES composition (applicable to this sample) was calculated as 1638 K by a machine-learning approach and 1620 K by the rule of mixture.
